chapters.summary: Sundara: Hanuman leaps the ocean, passes Surasa and Simhika, overcomes Lanka's guardian, finds Sita in the Ashoka grove and proclaims Rama's victory.

signs.text: The mansion of Kumbhakarna. His snoring shakes the golden walls; he sleeps for months at a time.
The house of Indrajit, Ravana's eldest son, who once defeated Indra himself.
The house of Prahasta, commander of Ravana's armies.
The hall of Pushpaka, the flying chariot Ravana took from his brother Kubera.
The house of Vibhishana, Ravana's younger brother. A quiet lamp burns inside, and someone is praying.

cmds.say: Hanuman stands on the summit of Mahendra. He presses down with his feet, and the whole mountain trembles.
Rama, Lakshmana and Sugriva return to Kishkindha to wait for news. Jambavan stays with the vanaras on the shore.

then.say: Only Hanuman can make this crossing. You ride on his shoulder and guide his steps.
The vanaras hold their breath. Hanuman crouches low, ready to spring.

cmds.say: Only Hanuman can make this crossing. You hold the verse book tight and go with him, a witness carried on the wind.
Hanuman springs into the sky, and the ocean opens beneath you, blue and endless.

cmds.objective: Fly east across the ocean to Lanka.

cmds.say: Provisions for the crossing! Fruit, roots, honey and herbs. Lanka will not sell you any.
Go, Hanuman! The whole army is watching you!
Midway across the {n:place.ocean_leap}, a golden mountain rises out of the waves: Mainaka.
Rest on my peak, son of the Wind. Your father once saved me, and I would honour you.
Hanuman touches the peak with his hand in thanks. 'I have promised not to stop,' he says gently.
While he speaks with the mountain, you kneel at an old shrine on its slope and catch your breath.
Your party is fully rested. The shrine on Mainaka will keep your place.
A vast serpent-woman rises from the sea and blocks the way: Surasa, mother of serpents.
The gods have sent me to test you. None may pass me without entering my mouth.
Then let wit go where strength cannot.

onWin.say: Surasa opens her mouth wider and wider. Hanuman grows to match her, then suddenly shrinks to the size of a thumb.
He darts into her mouth and out again before she can close it, and bows to her.
Go, best of vanaras. Find Sita, and bring Rama joy.

onLose.say: Surasa waits, unmoved. Think again, son of the Wind.

cmds.say: You fall back toward Mainaka. Its shrine will restore you.

then.say: Then open your mouth wide, and I will enter.
Surasa opens her mouth wide, and Hanuman grows. She opens it wider, and he grows again.

then.choice: Her mouth is vast now. What should Hanuman do?

then.say: Hanuman grows once more, and Surasa only opens her mouth wider. She waits.
Suddenly Hanuman becomes as small as a thumb.
He darts into her mouth and out again before she can close it, and bows to her.
Go, best of vanaras. Find Sita, and bring Rama joy.

cmds.say: Suddenly Hanuman slows, as if caught. Something beneath the waves has seized his shadow!
It is Simhika, who drags down flying creatures by their shadows.

onWin.say: Hanuman breaks free, and Simhika sinks beneath the waves, never to trouble travellers again.
Ahead, the shore of Lanka appears, green with forests and bright with golden towers.

onWin.objective: Land on the shore of Lanka, to the east.

cmds.say: The waves are wild here. Fly on carefully.
Hanuman lands softly on Lamba hill. Before him rises Lanka on Mount Trikuta, its golden walls shining like a city of the gods.
He waits for night. Then he makes himself as small as a cat, to slip inside unseen.
An old stone shrine stands on the hillside to the west, forgotten by the city. You may rest there.

cmds.objective: Enter the city gate to the north.

cmds.say: A fearsome figure bars the gate: Lanka herself, the guardian goddess of the city.
Who are you, creeping into my city by night? Turn back, or I will destroy you.
I only wish to see your city. Let me pass.

cmds.choice: Rest and save before the battle?

battle.intro: Lanka, guardian of the city, blocks the gate!

onWin.say: Hanuman strikes her with his left fist, holding back his strength, for she is a woman. Lanka sinks to her knees.
Long ago Brahma told me: when a vanara overcomes you, know that the end of the rakshasas is near. That time has come.
Enter, and find what you seek.

onWin.objective: Search the city of Lanka for Sita.

cmds.say: The great gate of Lanka is shut, and its guardian stands before it.
{n:place.lanka_city} by night: golden mansions, crystal stairs, music and lamps in every window.
Small as a cat, Hanuman slips from house to house, searching every face for Sita.

then.say: Lamps light the streets, and guards watch the light. Lead Hanuman through the dark.

cmds.objective: Search the city. Ravana's palace lies to the north.

then.say: A patrol marches past the palace gate. Small as a cat, Hanuman waits in the dark, and they never see him.
The patrol is gone. The street is quiet.

else.say: Night-wanderers on patrol spot a strange little monkey on the avenue!

onWin.say: The patrol scatters into the dark lanes.

then.say: The guard peers into the dark, but sees nothing.
The patrol is gone. The street is quiet.

else.say: A yatudhana guarding the west lane sniffs the air. 'I smell a stranger!'

onWin.say: The patrol scatters into the dark lanes.

then.say: The guards at the garden wall look the other way. Hanuman slips past them.
The patrol is gone. The street is quiet.

else.say: Guards at the eastern gardens raise their spears!

onWin.say: The patrol scatters into the dark lanes.

cmds.say: Pearls, silks, sandalwood! Lanka never sleeps.
She does not notice the small monkey slipping past her stall.
The guard snores against the wall, his spear across his knees.
Hanuman searches Ravana's palace: the halls, the gardens, the flying chariot Pushpaka, every sleeping chamber. Sita is not there.
Have I failed? If I return without news, Rama will lose hope, and so will everyone who loves him.
Hanuman sits on the palace wall, his head bowed. Then he lifts it.
No. Despair is not the way. {w:anirveda} is the root of all {w:shri}.

onCorrect.say: Well read! You can see how each word plays its part in the sentence.

onWrong.say: Not quite. Look at the word's ending; it tells you its role.

cmds.say: There is one place I have not searched: the Ashoka grove beyond the palace, to the east.

cmds.objective: Go east to the Ashoka grove.

cmds.say: A high golden wall encloses a fragrant garden. Hanuman resolves to search Ravana's palace first.
In the Ashoka grove, under a shimshapa tree, sits a lady in a faded yellow garment, pale with grief, guarded by rakshasis.
Hanuman knows at once: this is Sita, just as Rama described her.
Hiding among the branches, he watches. At dawn Ravana comes with threats and promises.
Sita places a blade of grass between herself and Ravana and answers him with courage. She will not even look at him.
Ravana storms away. When the guards drift off to sleep, Hanuman begins to speak, softly, from the tree.

then.say: The fire has not touched the grove. Sita is unharmed.
Hanuman, you are unhurt! Go now, and bring Rama soon.
Hanuman bows to her once more. Then he climbs a hill by the sea and leaps for home.
In the honey grove, Madhuvana, the vanaras sing, dance and tumble from the trees.
Stop! This is the king's own grove!
But Angada has told them to drink, and the dance goes on.
Dadhimukha, keeper of Sugriva's honey grove, runs to the king: the vanaras have drunk all the honey!
Sugriva laughs. He knows at once: they have found Sita.
At Kishkindha, Hanuman bowed to Rama. 'I have seen Sita.'
He placed her jewel in Rama's hands.
It is as if I see her again. Hanuman, what can I ever give you in return?
Sugriva ordered the whole army to march. Within days, the vanaras camped on the southern shore of the ocean.

then.objective: Rejoin Rama at the shore camp to begin Book 6.

then.say: Go safely, Hanuman. Tell Rama I am waiting for him.
From the branches, Hanuman sings Rama's story softly, and you sing it with him.
The princes of Ayodhya go to the forest.
A golden deer appears in the forest.
Ravana carries Sita away, and Rama searches for her.
Rama finds a friend in Sugriva, and the search begins.

else.say: From the branches, Hanuman sings Rama's story softly: the princes of Ayodhya, the exile, the golden deer, Rama's grief, the friendship with Sugriva, the search.
Who speaks Rama's name in this place? Am I dreaming?
Sita's heart lifts. An old saying comes to her mind, and now it seems true.

onCorrect.say: Yes! {w:ananda}, long awaited, reaches Sita at last.

onWrong.say: Not quite. Read the word card again; this verse is full of hope.

else.say: Hanuman climbs down and bows low.
I am Hanuman, Rama's messenger. Here is his ring, engraved with his name.
Sita holds the ring, and her eyes fill with tears of joy, as if she had met Rama himself.

then.choice: Sita asks you: "When will Rama come?"

options.label: With Sugriva and all the vanaras.
Soon. Hanuman will take him the news, and then he will come.

then.say: From Kishkindha... yes. But when, child? When?
With an army of vanaras! But when will he come?
Soon... I will hold on to that word.

else.say: My lady, sit on my back. I will carry you across the ocean to Rama this very hour.
No, Hanuman. Rama himself must come and win me back, as befits his honour.
Take this jewel from my hair. Rama will know it, and know that I live.
Tell Rama I will wait only a little longer. Go safely.

else.objective: Climb the temple steps in the north-east of the grove.

then.say: Something has changed. The lady smiles for the first time.
She keeps whispering an old saying: joy does come to one who stays alive, even if it takes a hundred years.
{w:ananda}, joy. I think it has found her at last.

else.say: I am Trijata. Last night I dreamt of Rama in white garlands and of Lanka sinking into the sea.
I told the others: do not threaten this lady. Ask her forgiveness instead.

cmds.say: The rakshasi guard is fast asleep.
The guard yawns, rubs her eyes, and dozes off again.
Before leaving, Hanuman decides to test the strength of Ravana's army.
He breaks the boughs of Ravana's pleasure grove, climbs the temple, and roars a challenge over the city.
And he names himself Rama's {w:dasa}, so that all Lanka will know who has come.
The mightiest warrior in Lanka tonight calls himself a {w:dasa}, a servant. That is how Hanuman serves Rama.
Rakshasa soldiers pour toward the grove! Hanuman waits on the temple steps.

cmds.objective: Restore the victory verse on the temple steps.

cmds.say: On the temple steps you raise your voice with Hanuman's, so the victory verse rings out whole.

then.say: The verse shines gold! Hanuman's victory cry, {n:move.jaya_ghosha}, is yours to call on in battle.
The temple shrine stands just above you. Rest there before the battle.

then.objective: Face Ravana's army beyond the east gate of the grove.

else.say: A few words slipped. Step away, gather yourself, and climb the steps to try again.

else.objective: Restore the victory verse on the temple steps.

then.say: Soldiers gather beyond the gate. Restore the victory verse on the temple steps first.

else.say: The eastern gate of the grove is barred. Hanuman has not finished here.

cmds.say: Ravana sent his servants against Hanuman, then his generals, then the sons of his ministers. All of them fell back.
Now Ravana's young son Aksha rides out in a golden chariot, bright as fire.
A monkey dares to break my father's garden? You will not leave Lanka.

cmds.choice: Rest and save before the battle?

onWin.say: Aksha falls in battle, and all Lanka trembles.
Then Indrajit, Ravana's eldest son, bound Hanuman with the weapon of Brahma. Out of respect for Brahma, Hanuman let himself be taken, to see Ravana face to face.
In Ravana's court Hanuman gave Rama's message: return Sita, and live. Ravana ordered his death, but Vibhishana reminded him that a messenger must never be killed.
So the rakshasas wrapped Hanuman's tail in cloth and set it on fire.

then.say: But the fire does not burn him, for Sita has prayed to Agni for his safety. Hanuman breaks free and springs onto the roofs.

then.objective: Leap from roof to roof with Hanuman's blazing tail.

onWin.say: With his blazing tail Hanuman leapt from roof to roof, and Lanka burned. The fire did not hurt him, for Sita had prayed to Agni for his safety.
Afraid for Sita, he hurried back to the grove and found her unharmed. He bowed to her once more, and leapt for home.
At Kishkindha, Hanuman bowed to Rama. 'I have seen Sita.'
He placed her jewel in Rama's hands.
It is as if I see her again. Hanuman, what can I ever give you in return?
Sugriva ordered the whole army to march. Within days, the vanaras camped on the southern shore of the ocean.

onWin.objective: Rejoin Rama at the shore camp to begin Book 6.

then.say: A guard turns toward the light! Hanuman slips back into the shadows.
A guard turns toward the light! Hanuman slips back into the shadows.
A guard turns toward the light! Hanuman slips back into the shadows.
A guard turns toward the light! Hanuman slips back into the shadows.
A guard turns toward the light! Hanuman slips back into the shadows.
Prahasta's house catches fire!
Only Vibhishana's house is spared.
Hanuman dips his tail in the sea, and the fire goes out. Then fear grips him: is Sita safe?

then.objective: Go to Sita in the Ashoka grove.

else.objective: Leap from roof to roof with Hanuman's blazing tail.

then.say: Kumbhakarna's mansion catches fire!
Only Vibhishana's house is spared.
Hanuman dips his tail in the sea, and the fire goes out. Then fear grips him: is Sita safe?

then.objective: Go to Sita in the Ashoka grove.

then.say: Mansion after mansion goes up in flames.
Only Vibhishana's house is spared.
Hanuman dips his tail in the sea, and the fire goes out. Then fear grips him: is Sita safe?

then.objective: Go to Sita in the Ashoka grove.

else.objective: Leap from roof to roof with Hanuman's blazing tail.

then.say: Last of all, Ravana's own palace catches fire!
Only Vibhishana's house is spared.
Hanuman dips his tail in the sea, and the fire goes out. Then fear grips him: is Sita safe?

then.objective: Go to Sita in the Ashoka grove.
